questions_and_answers.question: When you answer the phone for the American Embassy, what is the first thing you will say?

answers.answer: (Greeting) Amerika Taishikan de gozaimasu. (This is the American Embassy.)

questions_and_answers.question: If you are answering in the visa section, what will your first utterance be?
What is the Japanese word for 'visa' used here?
How may the caller ask for your boss?

answers.answer: By saying '...san onegai shimasu' or by giving only the title (and ...san)
By giving the extension number only

questions_and_answers.question: Why are you supposed to use more polite (or more humble) expressions when you answer the phone?

answers.answer: Because the Japanese think you are answering the phone on behalf of your office
Because the phone connection is poor
Because casual speech is forbidden by law

questions_and_answers.question: Which is more appropriate when answering a business call: 'de gozaimasu' or 'desu'?

answers.answer: de gozaimasu (it is more polite than desu)
desu (it is more polite than de gozaimasu)
They are exactly equal in politeness

questions_and_answers.question: Which is more appropriate: 'Shooshoo omachi kudasai' or 'Chotto matte kudasai'?

answers.answer: Shooshoo omachi kudasai (it is more polite)
Chotto matte kudasai (it is more polite)
Neither is appropriate on the phone

questions_and_answers.question: What does the greeting expression at the start signal in a business answer like '(Greeting) Amerika Taishikan de gozaimasu'?

answers.answer: A polite opening (e.g., a time-of-day greeting) before identifying the office
A request for the caller's name
An apology for a wrong number

questions_and_answers.question: Where will the discussion of more polite (and more humble) expressions used in telephone conversations continue?

articles.text:
2. How to answer a call in your office

What has been discussed above also applies when you answer a call in your office. For example, if you answer the phone for the American Embassy, the first thing you will say is:

(Greeting) Amerika Taishikan de gozaimasu.    (Greeting) This is the American Embassy.

If you are answering in the visa section, your first utterance will be:

Sashoo-ka de gozaimasu.    The visa section.

(Sashoo is the Japanese word for 'visa'.)

The caller may ask for your boss by saying ...san onegai shimasu. Alternatively, s/he may ask for your boss by giving only his/her title (and ...san). What is important is that you are supposed to use more polite (or more humble) expressions when you answer the phone. This is because the Japanese think you are answering the phone on behalf of your office.

Thus, de gozaimasu is more appropriate than desu. Likewise, Shooshoo omachi kudasai 'Please wait a moment' is more appropriate than Chotto matte kudasai. We will continue our discussion of more polite (and more humble) expressions used in telephone conversations in the next lesson.
